summary: BLM lookout on Chinks (Chinese) Peak near Pocatello, Idaho: station from 1944, 1962 concrete cab, 1957 arson fire, listed destroyed in 2003 (one site says removed).

facts.design: Two-story concrete and frame cab with flat inverted windows, built 1962; it replaced a two-story 10x10-foot cab from 1947
facts.status_note: Two lookout sites list the cab as destroyed in 2003; the Forest Lookouts page lists the 2003 event as removed (Kresek)

staffing.status: Cecil and Lillie Dixon listed 1948-1966; Robert and Sandra Rands 1967; newspapers report Cecil Dixon's return for 1968 and his presence on the peak in 1969

access.note: The climbing guide describes a road from south Pocatello to the summit, and a BLM gate with trailhead parking 1.8 miles up Barton Road; it gives no closure notice. No source describes access to the former lookout site now.

visit.trail_note: Barton Road from the south side of Pocatello, 4.7 miles to the summit, per the climbing guide. No source describes what remains of the cab.

events.note: A new lookout station was established on the peak after a fire road was built to the top; the structure is not described
Two-story 10x10-foot cab, per the lookout websites
Cecil and Lillie Dixon are listed as staff from 1948 to 1966
BLM brought a modern trailer up the peak by bulldozer as living quarters
A fire burned down the 12-by-12-foot watch station; county officers suspected arson
A June 1958 newspaper said the station would get its first direct telephone line; in November 1958 BLM proposed withdrawing 80 acres for lookout and radio facilities
A January 1960 report mentions reconstruction of the lookout; the newspaper does not give the size of the rebuild
Two-story concrete and frame cab with flat inverted windows replaced the 1947 cab
Robert and Sandra Rands replaced the Dixons as the BLM's fire watchers
Cecil Dixon was announced to return to the lookout after a year away
Vandalism found in early June 1968 smashed one side of the glass cab and demolished the downstairs door; when it happened is not known; teenagers were blamed
As a Pocatello-area cooperative fire contract was being ended, the BLM said it would keep maintaining the lookout
The Geographic Names Information System changed the name from Chinks Peak to Chinese Peak
Listed as destroyed by the lookout websites; the Forest Lookouts page lists it as removed (Kresek)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Two lookout sites say the cab was destroyed in 2003; the Forest Lookouts page says Removed (Kresek). The story reports both and does not pick one, because the sources give no detail.
The staff lists end the Dixons in 1966, but newspapers quoted on the Forest Lookouts page report Cecil Dixon's return for 1968 and show him on the peak in 1969. The story follows the newspaper dates.

The 1957 newspaper describes a 12-by-12-foot watch station, while the lookout sites give the 1947 cab as 10 by 10 feet. Not resolved: the sources do not say whether these are the same building, so the story says the accounts may differ.

notes_for_editor: The brief's height_m 3.7 is not supported by any of the five sources read, so it is left out of facts; check before publishing. The 2003 fate is disputed (destroyed vs removed) and no source gives detail. Access 'public' rests on the climbing guide's road description and Wikipedia's road/bike trail line; no closure notice was found. Staffing dates from newspapers quoted on the Forest Lookouts page, which the staff lists omit. A 2020 wildfire on the peak appeared in search results (eastidahonews.com); it was not read or used because nothing ties it to the lookout. No new photos were found. Search budget: one WebSearch.
